title: 10 Best Microsoft Teams Ticketing Systems (2026)
summary: Microsoft Teams is where employees already ask for help. Compare the ten best Teams ticketing systems for 2026, what each is built for, and how to judge integration depth, AI and private workflows.
body_markdown:
10 Best Microsoft Teams Ticketing Systems Compared for 2026' with the Unthread logo at top left. On the right, illustrated UI cards show a Microsoft Teams IT Support channel where a message reading


Microsoft Teams has become a central hub for workplace communication, with[320 million monthly users](https://www.businessofapps.com/data/microsoft-teams-statistics/) . Yet many organizations still require employees to leave Teams when they need IT support, HR assistance, or help from other internal teams. That context switching can make requests harder to track and route consistently.


A[Teams ticketing system](https://unthread.io/products/microsoft-teams-support) brings structured help desk workflows into the collaboration tools employees already use. Teams can turn conversations into trackable tickets with assignments, SLAs, routing, private workflows, and automation while keeping the employee experience conversational.


**Key Takeaways**


- Unthread is designed for organizations that want internal support across Microsoft Teams, Slack, email, and other intake channels in one workflow.
- ServiceNow, Freshservice, and Jira Service Management suit organizations that need broader ITSM processes alongside Microsoft Teams.
- Teams-focused tools such as Desk365, Tikit, and TeamsWork provide ticketing workflows built around Microsoft's collaboration ecosystem.
- AI agents can answer routine employee questions, route requests, trigger workflows, and escalate issues that require human attention.
- Private request flows matter for HR, IT, finance, and other teams handling sensitive employee information.
- Organizations should evaluate integration depth, automation, administration requirements, and multi-department support rather than focusing on ticket creation alone.


## **What to Look for in a Teams Ticketing System**


Before comparing individual platforms, internal support teams should consider how deeply each option fits their existing workflows.


**Integration depth:** A[Teams ticketing system](https://unthread.io/products/microsoft-teams-support) should do more than send notifications. Employees should be able to submit requests naturally, while support teams can assign, route, update, and resolve them with minimal context switching.


**AI automation:** AI agents can answer common employee questions, reference internal knowledge, triage requests, draft responses, and trigger workflows before a human agent needs to intervene.


**Multi-channel support:** Organizations using both Microsoft Teams and Slack may need a unified system that consolidates requests from multiple collaboration tools, email, and other intake channels.


**Private workflows:** HR, finance, legal, and IT teams frequently handle sensitive requests. A suitable platform should support private conversations and controlled ticket visibility.


**Workflow flexibility:** Routing rules, approvals, escalations, and[automations](https://unthread.io/products/automations) change as organizations grow. Admins should consider how much effort is required to create and adjust those processes.


## **1) Unthread: Best for AI-Native Internal Support**


**Best for:** Organizations that want to manage employee support across Microsoft Teams, Slack, email, and other intake channels while automating Tier 1 internal service workflows.


**Price:** $50 per agent/month on the annual Basic plan and $75 per agent/month on the annual Pro plan, with a minimum of five seats.


Unthread is an[AI-native internal help desk](https://unthread.io/) built around conversational employee support. Instead of requiring employees to learn a separate service portal, it turns conversations from Microsoft Teams, Slack,[email](https://unthread.io/products/shared-email-inbox) , and other channels into structured requests that internal teams can track, route, and resolve.


Its purpose-built AI agent can support Tier 1 workflows across IT,[HR](https://unthread.io/solutions/hr-service-desk) , finance, procurement, legal, and workplace operations. Unthread reports that Lemonade uses its automation across multiple departments and achieves about[40% automatic resolution](https://unthread.io/customers) .


The platform is also designed to give administrators flexibility as internal processes change. Routing rules, escalations, knowledge workflows, and automations can be configured without rebuilding the underlying service desk.


### **Key Features**


- Purpose-built AI agent for answering, triaging, routing, and resolving internal requests
- [Knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base) that can draft documentation from resolved conversations
- [Agentic AI](https://unthread.io/products/agentic-ai) with MCP support for bring-your-own-LLM environments
- [Workflow automations](https://unthread.io/products/automations) created through natural language, a visual builder, or custom functions
- Private flows for HR and other sensitive employee requests
- Multi-channel intake across Teams, Slack, email, and other support surfaces
- Integrations with Jira, Zendesk, Salesforce, ServiceNow, and other business systems


### **Pros**


- Supports multiple internal departments rather than a single IT workflow
- Consolidates requests from Teams, Slack, and other channels
- AI automation can handle routine requests before escalation
- Admins can adjust routing and workflows as processes evolve


## **2) ServiceNow**


ServiceNow is an enterprise service management platform for organizations that need structured ITSM processes alongside Microsoft Teams. Its broader platform covers areas such as incident management, service requests, workflows, approvals, asset-related processes, and employee service delivery, making it relevant to organizations with formal service management requirements.


### **Key Features**


- Incident and request management workflows
- Approval and escalation processes
- Enterprise service management across multiple departments
- Microsoft Teams access to service workflows
- Knowledge management and automation
- Broader IT operations and asset management capabilities


### **Pros**


- Supports complex enterprise service management environments
- Covers processes beyond basic ticketing
- Can connect Teams-based employee interactions with established ITSM workflows


### **Considerations**


- Implementation and administration requirements can be substantial
- Organizations primarily seeking lightweight conversational ticketing may not need the full platform scope


## **3) Freshservice**


Freshservice is Freshworks' IT service management platform for internal IT and employee service workflows. Organizations can use its Microsoft Teams capabilities to give employees a conversational route into service management while maintaining structured tickets and ITSM processes in Freshservice.


### **Key Features**


- Microsoft Teams service interactions
- Incident and service request management
- Freddy AI capabilities
- Knowledge management
- Workflow automation
- IT asset and service management features


### **Pros**


- Combines conversational employee access with established ITSM processes
- Supports common incident and request workflows
- Includes automation and AI functionality within the broader Freshservice platform


### **Considerations**


- Its broader ITSM scope may be more than smaller internal support teams require
- Teams is one interface into the service desk rather than the platform's sole operating environment


## **4) Jira Service Management**


Jira Service Management is Atlassian's service management platform for IT, engineering, operations, and other internal teams. It is particularly relevant to organizations already using Jira and other Atlassian products that want employee requests connected to engineering and operational workflows.


### **Key Features**


- Incident, request, problem, and change management
- Jira-based workflow customization
- Knowledge management through the Atlassian ecosystem
- Automation and approval workflows
- Microsoft Teams collaboration options
- Connections between service requests and engineering work


### **Pros**


- Fits organizations already working heavily in Jira
- Connects service management with development and operations workflows
- Provides configurable request and approval processes


### **Considerations**


- Teams interactions form part of a broader Jira Service Management workflow
- Organizations without an existing Atlassian footprint may have less reason to adopt the wider ecosystem


## **5) Desk365**


Desk365 focuses on help desk workflows within Microsoft Teams. It provides separate experiences for employees submitting requests and agents managing tickets, making it relevant to organizations that want Microsoft Teams to remain the primary interface for internal support.


### **Key Features**


- Support and agent experiences within Teams
- Message-to-ticket conversion
- Ticket assignments and status management
- Microsoft Entra ID support
- AI-assisted categorization and response workflows


### **Pros**


- Strong emphasis on Microsoft Teams workflows
- Employees can create requests without adopting another communication tool
- Provides structured ticket management around Teams conversations


### **Considerations**


- Organizations using both Slack and Teams may need broader multi-channel coverage
- Its positioning is more Teams-focused than platforms built for unified intake across several collaboration channels


## **6) Tikit**


Tikit by Cireson is a Microsoft-focused service desk designed for organizations already operating heavily within Microsoft 365. It connects Teams ticketing with other Microsoft technologies, making it relevant when internal support workflows are closely tied to the Microsoft ecosystem.


### **Key Features**


- Message-to-ticket workflows in Teams
- Adaptive Cards for ticket interactions
- Connections with Microsoft Entra and Power Automate
- Knowledge-based request handling
- Internal service workflows across multiple departments


### **Pros**


- Closely aligned with Microsoft 365 environments
- Supports service workflows directly from Teams
- Can connect ticketing with other Microsoft tools


### **Considerations**


- Organizations with mixed Slack and Teams environments may prefer a platform designed for both
- Some administration and service management activities may extend beyond the Teams interface


## **7) TeamsWork**


TeamsWork provides ticketing applications designed to operate within Microsoft Teams. It can support departmental ticketing for functions such as IT, HR, facilities, and other internal teams while allowing employees to stay within the Microsoft collaboration environment.


### **Key Features**


- Teams-based ticket submission and tracking
- Multiple ticketing instances for different departments
- Support for internal approval processes
- Multi-language capabilities
- Microsoft 365-oriented deployment


### **Pros**


- Keeps employee request workflows closely connected to Teams
- Supports separate ticketing environments for different departments
- Can fit organizations seeking a focused Teams-based ticketing layer


### **Considerations**


- AI automation is not the primary focus compared with AI-native internal help desks
- Organizations requiring broad third-party workflow orchestration may need to evaluate integration depth carefully


## **8) SysAid**


SysAid is an established[IT service management platform](https://unthread.io/solutions/it-service-desk) that brings service desk and automation capabilities into Microsoft Teams. It is suited to organizations that need formal IT service processes together with conversational employee access.


### **Key Features**


- Incident and service request management
- AI-assisted ticket categorization
- Approval workflows
- Asset management
- Problem and change management
- Conversational service access through Teams


### **Pros**


- Supports a broad range of traditional ITSM processes
- Combines service desk and asset management capabilities
- Provides structured workflows for larger IT organizations


### **Considerations**


- Its broader ITSM feature set can require more administration than a focused Teams ticketing tool
- Cross-department internal support requirements should be evaluated against its IT-oriented workflows


## **9) InvGate Service Management**


InvGate Service Management provides ITSM workflows for organizations that want structured incident, request, problem, and change management. Its Microsoft Teams capabilities give employees another channel for accessing the service desk without replacing the broader InvGate environment.


### **Key Features**


- Virtual Service Agent in Microsoft Teams
- Incident and service request workflows
- Knowledge-based answers
- Approval processes
- ITIL-aligned service management
- Automation and reporting


### **Pros**


- Provides formal ITSM workflows alongside Teams access
- Supports conversational entry into service requests
- Covers multiple core service management processes


### **Considerations**


- Teams acts as an access channel rather than the entire service management environment
- Organizations primarily seeking lightweight multi-department conversational support may need fewer ITSM capabilities


## **10) Pylon**


Pylon is a conversational support platform with capabilities for managing requests that originate in collaboration channels. Its focus is primarily B2B customer support rather than employee-facing IT, HR, finance, or workplace service delivery, so its fit depends on whether Microsoft Teams is being used for external or internal conversations.


### **Key Features**


- Conversation-based request management
- Routing and assignment workflows
- Support for shared collaboration channels
- AI-assisted support processes
- Multi-channel communication management


### **Pros**


- Supports conversational workflows in collaboration channels
- Can help teams structure requests without replacing the conversational experience
- Relevant to organizations managing B2B support conversations in shared channels


### **Considerations**


- Its primary use case is external customer support rather than internal service management
- Organizations focused on employee IT, HR, finance, or workplace requests may prefer a platform built specifically for internal support

> **Frequently Asked Questions**


**What is a Microsoft Teams ticketing system?**


A Microsoft Teams ticketing system turns employee conversations and requests into structured tickets with assignments, statuses, SLAs, routing, and workflows. Depending on the platform, employees may be able to submit and follow requests directly from Teams while internal support teams manage the underlying service process.


**How does an AI agent improve a Teams help desk?**


A purpose-built AI agent can answer routine questions from internal knowledge, triage incoming requests, route tickets, draft responses, trigger workflows, and escalate issues that require human attention. This can help internal teams spend more time on requests that require judgment or specialized work.


**Can existing ITSM tools work with Teams ticketing?**


Yes. Many Teams ticketing platforms connect with existing ITSM and business systems. Unthread, for example, supports[enterprise integrations](https://unthread.io/products/integrations) with tools including Jira, Zendesk, Salesforce, and ServiceNow, allowing Teams-based intake to work alongside existing operational systems.


**What are the benefits of a Teams-based help desk?**


A Teams-based help desk lets employees request assistance within a collaboration environment they already use. It can reduce context switching while giving internal teams structured ticketing, routing, assignments, SLAs, automation, and reporting behind the conversational experience.


**How can sensitive HR requests be handled in Teams?**


Internal support platforms can use private ticketing flows for requests involving payroll, parental leave, benefits, employee documents, or policy questions. Unthread supports private workflows that let employees contact the appropriate[HR service desk](https://unthread.io/solutions/hr-service-desk) while keeping sensitive requests separate from public channels.
